title: Thin-Crust Lemon Pizza with Black Pepper and Crème Fraîche
changes_from_base: Overlapping paper-thin lemon slices with black pepper and olive oil bake on a very thin crust in place of tomato sauce and mozzarella, and cool crème fraîche and chives go on after baking; the salmon roe in the original is left out.
summary: Tissue-thin crust topped with translucent lemon slices that caramelise slightly in the oven, finished with cooling crème fraîche and herbaceous chives.
equipment: pizza stone or rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: pizza dough, shop-bought or homemade, at room temperature
lemons, ends trimmed, sliced paper-thin, pips removed

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Set the oven to 230 °C (place a pizza stone inside if you have one; if using a tray, brush it lightly with 5 ml oil).

steps.title: Roll thin
steps.text: Roll the 340 g dough very thinly to about 4 mm thickness and roughly 30 cm across, then transfer to the tray or a floured peel.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Cover the entire base with thin, overlapping slices of the 3 lemons (pips removed), grind ½ tsp ground black pepper across the surface and drizzle with 15 ml oil.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the base becomes brown and crisp; if the lemon begins to brown too quickly, lay foil loosely across the top.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Allow the pizza to cool slightly, spread 120 g crème fraîche over the surface and scatter the 2 tbsp finely chopped chives across the top.

tips: Roll the dough extremely thin so the base crisps properly underneath the lemon weight
Cover with foil if the lemon is browning faster than the crust is cooking to prevent the citrus from charring
Remove the pips from lemon slices before topping so diners don't bite into bitter seeds
storage: Keep leftovers chilled and eat within 1 day. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
